***DISCLAIMER*** Although I said you can hoop in the Sambas DOES NOT mean that you SHOULD hoop in Sambas. So if any of y’all try this out and injure yourself, you only have yourselves to blame. I do these videos with risk to my own health and safety so that you guys don’t have to put your own body at risk. Although the Sambas have good performance for basketball standards, it definitely should not be considered as your main basketball shoe. I think this disclaimer should be pretty self explanatory but there’s a lot of you that probably won’t read this and come at me in the comments section anyways but oh well.  But this is one of Adidas’ most popular and best indoor soccer (Futsal) shoes of all time and has gained a reputation as such over the years. There are Samba models that are more tailored towards Futsal like the Samba Classic as it comes with a more traditional tongue for the sport and would honestly perform better for basketball as well.  As cliche as this saying has become, these really did remind me of a Kobe shoe. Minus the cushioning and other supportive features that those normally have of course. Kobe was really onto something when he brought idea to his design team about making his shoes similar to soccer shoes. In his words Kobe said in reference to having his shoes low-cut like soccer shoes: “When you see a soccer player, they do twice as much torque on their ankles as we do [basketball players] and they’re able to manage just fine.” And Kobe really debunked the myth that all basketball shoes needed to be high tops.
